text:
Mia Patel: Heads up — customer returned a redline that adds an MFN + price protection clause. They're asking that we match any better commercial terms offered to other customers for 12 months. Link to redline: https://redwood.internal/ctrl/RC-8674/redline v3
Raj Kapoor: Do they ask for retroactive matching or only future offers? Any carve-outs in their language?
Emily Chen: Legal: initial read — it's broad. We can push to narrow: exclude marketplace/promos/trials/pilots, exclude resellers, and cap duration to 12 months. Suggest language: 'MFN limited to substantially similar enterprise offers; excludes marketplace promotions, trials, pilots, and partner reseller arrangements.'
Jordan Lee: From POC/SE POV — if POC pricing is covered by MFN we lose conversion leverage. We should explicitly exclude POCs or require separate conversion pricing with defined acceptance criteria.
Carlos Medina: Deal Desk: need current rate card and proposed commit/discount matrix to model impact. Broad MFN + retroactive matching could force us to honor lower prices and blow unit economics.
Mia Patel: Customer is pushing MFN as standard for them. @deal-desk @finance can you weigh in quickly? Is a 12mo cap + exclusions a deal-breaker? :eyes:
Contracts Bot: Automated: RC-8674 redline uploaded by customer (v3). Uploaded by acustomer@example.com. SHA256: 3f1b9a...
Emily Chen: We can accept with modifications: 12mo duration, explicit exclusions for POCs/trials/marketplace/resellers, and a definition of 'substantially similar' (same product family + comparable SLA + similar committed volume). We should also add a discount cap to avoid unlimited downside.
Raj Kapoor: Pricing Ops note — any clause that references 'published list price' or 'public rate card' ties us to freezes. A price cap may require us to forego certain promotional levers. Finance sign-off required.
Carlos Medina: Deal Desk proposal: MFN limited to published list price for equivalent committed volume; discount cap = 30%; commit threshold >= $100k ARR for MFN to apply. Otherwise MFN doesn't kick in. That protects margins.
Mia Patel: Customer is willing to negotiate commit size but wants MFN on any comparable enterprise deal. Can Sales offer 9-12mo protection, 25% discount cap, and explicit POC exclusion?
Emily Chen: Legal is comfortable with 12mo + exclusions + 30% cap. I'll prepare counter redline with that language and ask customer to sign.
Jordan Lee: SE: Confirm we add POC conversion terms (conversion price = defined %-of-committed-rate or explicit list price) and acceptance criteria documented in SOW.
Carlos Medina: Deal Desk: conditional approval. We need formal finance approval on the commit threshold and discount impact before final sign. Assigning to @finance. :white_check_mark:
Mia Patel: Thanks everyone — I'll prepare the counter (12mo MFN, exclude POC/trials/marketplace/resellers, 30% discount cap, MFN applies only if commit >= $100k ARR) and circulate. Any last objections?
Emily Chen: No objections from Legal. Proceed and attach updated redline.
Raj Kapoor: I'll run the pricing simulation once you post the final commit/discount numbers.
Mia Patel: Cool — pinging customer now and will update this thread after finance sign-off.
